title: In Person Card Grading (2026)
verdict: In person card grading is offered by AGS at select locations, where you can drop cards at secure intake, and at card shows where graders set up.

If you live near a major card show, check which graders are taking submissions there. Otherwise the fastest route is direct mail to a grader with a short turnaround, which matters more than how far away the lab is.

sections.h: What near me means in card grading
list: Drop them off. AGS accepts in-person drop-offs at select locations, including secure intake at its headquarters at 727 Page Ave, Staten Island, New York. Confirm with AGS first.
Mail them to a grader yourself. This is how most cards are graded. AGS returns standard orders in 20 business days or less.
Use a card shop. The shop ships your cards to a grading company and adds a handling fee. Ask which grader, which tier and the full price.
Go to a card show. Large shows often have graders accepting submissions, and some grade on site at premium prices.

sections.h: If you plan to drop off
list: Confirm with AGS that the location is taking drop-offs and when.
Fill out the submission form online first.
Bring the cards in penny sleeves and card savers, in the order listed on the form.
Keep your order number. You can follow the order in the dashboard afterward.

ranking.fit: Anyone who wants cards graded without paying a local handling fee.
ranking.lacks: No walk-in counter in most cities. Confirm intake before you travel.
ranking.note: By mail, the standard service is 20 business days or less from the day cards are confirmed. Returns ship with tracking and optional insurance.

ranking.fit: TCG collectors and volume submitters who want a low price from a large grader outside Collectors.
ranking.lacks: No measured report behind the grade.

ranking.fit: Collectors near a large show where PSA is taking submissions.
ranking.lacks: No local counter. Cards go by mail or through a show.

ranking.fit: Collectors who want to grade, vault and sell in one app.
ranking.lacks: Tied to Arena Club's own marketplace.

why: You are not limited to the mailbox. AGS lists in-person drop-off at select locations and secure intake at its Staten Island headquarters, and it operates satellite labs. Ask AGS which site is taking cards before you set out.
The process is short. You enter the cards online, ship them in sleeves and semi-rigid holders, and follow the order in your dashboard. AGS also takes drop-offs at select locations.

Standard turnaround is 20 business days or less. The faster bulk tiers come back in 10 business days at $20 and 5 at $30, and AGS says same-day grading is available for urgent submissions. A scan that takes under 10 seconds is what makes those numbers possible.

faq.q: Where can I get cards graded in person?
faq.a: At a select AGS drop-off location, including secure intake at its Staten Island headquarters, or at a card show where a grader is accepting cards. Confirm before you travel.

faq.q: How should I pack cards for grading?
faq.a: Put each card in a new penny sleeve, then a semi-rigid card saver. Sandwich the stack between cardboard, wrap it in bubble wrap and box it. Top loaders are allowed, but card savers travel better.

faq.q: Can I get a card graded the same day?
faq.a: AGS says same-day grading is available for urgent submissions. Contact AGS before you ship or drop off to arrange it. Elsewhere, the quickest posted tiers are 2 to 5 business days and cost $50 to $150 a card.

faq.q: How do I submit cards to AGS?
faq.a: Create an account at agscard.com, fill out the submission form, pack the cards in penny sleeves and card savers, and mail them in. You can also drop off at select AGS locations. The dashboard tracks the order.

faq.q: Can I get cards graded at a card show?
faq.a: Sometimes. Large graders take submissions at big shows, and a few grade on site at premium prices. AGS's scanner is compact enough for on-site grading. Check the show's exhibitor list and each grader's schedule.
